### Background

Using the machine learning algorithms that are taught in STAT 212: Statistical Machine learning, we can develop regression models that can predict future state based off of prior data. However, what the models in STAT 212 lack is a spacial component. What spacial machine learning models help us incorporate spacial relations into the model, having the regression of one space be dependent on both its prior trends and those of its neighbors.

For our project, we will be using a spacial machine learning algorithm because feral swine

### Running Spacial Machine Learning Algorithms

# Steps for Running Spacial Machine Learning Algorithms

## Step 1: Determine Spacial Autocorrelation

We first must determine spacial autocorrelation before we can even begin to run a spacial machine learning algorithm. Spacial autocorrelation determines if there is a spacial trend in out data or if there is a lack of trend. If there is a lack of a trend, we can not move on with running a spacial machine learning algorithm.

# Moran's I

Moran's I is a method of determining spacial autocorrelation.

```{r}
# Loading Packages
library(tidyverse)
library(spdep)
library(sf)
library(mapview)
library(sp)
library(rlist)
```

```{r}
# Loading Data
swine <- read_csv("../data/clean/combined_counties.csv")
us_county <- st_read("../data/raw/cb_2018_us_county_5m/cb_2018_us_county_5m.shp")
```

```{r}
# Making a dataset using only the contiguous United States without island counties
# Removing Nantucket County
us_48 <- us_county |> 
  filter(STATEFP != "15"& STATEFP != "11" & STATEFP != "02" & STATEFP != "72"
         & STATEFP != "78" & STATEFP != "60" & STATEFP != "66" & STATEFP != "69"
         & GEOID != "53055" & GEOID != "25019")

# Making a dataset of all counties in the united states with their swine presence
swine_counties = swine |> 
  select(county_ID, swine_2020, swine_2021, swine_2022, swine_2023, swine_2024, swine_2025) |> 
  mutate(across(where(is.logical), ~as.numeric(.x))) |> 
  right_join(us_48, join_by(county_ID == GEOID)) |> 
  mutate(swine_2020 = replace_na(swine_2020, 0),
         swine_2021 = replace_na(swine_2021, 0),
         swine_2022 = replace_na(swine_2022, 0),
         swine_2023 = replace_na(swine_2023, 0),
         swine_2024 = replace_na(swine_2024, 0),
         swine_2025 = replace_na(swine_2025, 0)) |> 
  st_as_sf(sf_column_name = "geometry") |> 
  as(Class ="Spatial")

# Mapping to see if the polygons work
mapview(swine_counties, zcol = "swine_2020")
```

```{r}
# Moran's I
nb <- poly2nb(swine_counties, queen = TRUE)

plot(nb,coordinates(swine_counties))

nbw <- nb2listw(nb, style = "W")

gmoran <- moran.test(swine_counties$swine_2020, nbw,alternative = "greater")
gmoran
```

### File Saving
```{r}
write.csv(swine_counties, "../data/clean/spatial_swine.csv")
write.csv(us_48, "../data/clean/lower_48.csv")
```
